items.title: Subjunctive use today
items.claim: The imparfait du subjonctif is widely described as moribund in modern French. In what context might it still appear?

options.text: In very formal literary writing, often for stylistic effect

items.reveal:
The form survives in writing for archaic or formal register. Spoken French typically uses the present subjunctive where the imperfect would be classical.

Grevisse's Le Bon Usage remains a standard reference describing the changing patterns.
items.why: Grammatical change is often gradual, leaving an archaic register that signals formality.

items.title: Languages spoken in France in 1789
items.claim: Abbe Gregoire's 1794 report estimated what proportion of French citizens spoke standard French as a native language at the time of the Revolution?
items.reveal_title: A small minority spoke standard French
items.reveal:
Gregoire's report 'Rapport sur la necessite et les moyens d'aneantir les patois' estimated that only around 3 million of 25 million inhabitants spoke French well; many used Occitan, Breton, Alsatian, Basque or other languages.

Universal primary education in the late 19th century did much of the standardisation.
items.why: Modern national languages are often the product of policy as much as organic spread.

items.title: Loi Toubon
items.claim: France's loi Toubon (1994) requires French in certain official contexts. Which is closest to what it covers?

options.text: It bans English speech in private homes
It requires French in commercial advertising, employment contracts and public-sector communication, with alternatives in foreign languages permitted but a French version also required
It applies only to government emails
It applies only to broadcast television

items.reveal_title: It mandates French in public commercial and administrative contexts
items.reveal:
The law was originally proposed by Jacques Toubon (then Minister of Culture). Some clauses were softened by the Constitutional Council on freedom-of-expression grounds.

Enforcement is sporadic but has produced occasional fines.
items.why: Language policy is most visible at the interface between commerce and state.
